 This Crp Is Filed Under Section 115 Of Code Of Civil
 Procedure, Praying To Call For Records And Set Aside The
 Order Dated 12.08.2014, Passed By The Learned Senior Civil
 Judge, Gangavathi, In Ep No.151/2012, Insofar It Opposes
 And Further Direct The Respondents To Pay The Due
 Amount As Per The Calculation Of The Petitioner Annexed
 To The E.P.No.151/2012, And Etc.,
 This Petition, Coming On For Final Hearing, This Day,

 Order

1. This petition by the petitioner/land looser/decree holder aggrieved by the order dated 12.08.2014 passed in EP No.151/2012 on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Gangavathi (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'Executing Court'), by which the Executing Court after making certain calculations of the decreetal amount has directed the respondents/Judgment Debtors No.1 and 2 to pay Rs.6,55,386/- within one month from the date of the order.

2. It is the case of the petitioner/land looser that;
(a) The land measuring 06 acres 20 guntas belonging to him was acquired on 04.09.1975 for the purpose of construction of APMC, Gangavathi.
Award was passed on 25.07.1986, possession taken on 26.11.1987.

A reference was made under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short,
hereinafter referred to as 'LA Act'), pursuant to which a case in LAC No.2/1988 came to be registered.

Compensation was determined at Rs.1.40 paisa per square feet payable to the land looser together NC: 2024:KHC-D:9816 with statutory payments namely, 30% solatium, 12% additional market value, 9% interest for the initial one year and 15% thereafter till the payment.
Consequence thereof, petitioner filed execution petition in EP No.538/1997 for recovery of a sum of Rs.18,65,441.20/-.
On payment of the amount so claimed in the said EP No.538/1997, the said execution petition was closed on 20.08.1998.

(b) Thereafter, in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sunder Vs.
Union of India reported in (2001) 7 SCC 211, petitioner filed another execution petition in EP No.58/2007 seeking recovery of Rs.20,59,911/- calculating interest on solatium and additional market value.

entities.text:
Sunder Vs.
Union of India reported in (2001) 7 SCC 211
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said execution petition was dismissed by order dated 30.06.2011.

Aggrieved by the same, petitioner had preferred a civil revision petition in CRP No.1115/2011 before this Court,
which came to be allowed by order dated 24.02.2012 setting aside the order dated 30.06.2011 passed in EP No.58/2007 and this Court NC: 2024:KHC-D:9816 held that the petitioner was entitled for interest on solatium and additional market value.
Shekhappa

2

(c) In view of the said order passed by this Court, a fresh execution petition in EP No.151/2012 (which is present execution petition) came to be filed by the petitioner/land looser claiming Rs.23,98,776/-.

While considering the said execution petition, the Executing Court made certain calculation and arrived at the conclusion that the petitioner/land looser is entitled for Rs.6,55,386/-
and accordingly directed the respondents to pay the same.
Being aggrieved by the same the petitioner is before this Court.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the calculation made by the Executing Court as seen at page No.12 of the impugned order is incorrect, irregular and erroneous.

He further submits that the method adopted by the Executing Court has resulted in substantial loss of pecuniary benefits to the petitioner/land looser, in that the Executing Court has not included the interest at NC: 2024:KHC-D:9816 the rate of 9% payable for the initial one year between 26.11.1986 and 25.11.1987 and has also not included 15% interest per annum payable after expiry of the said period of one year till payment.

(a) It is his further submission that any amount which was paid/payable by the respondent-authorities have to be adjusted firstly against the outstanding interest and thereafter against the principle amount.
This method of appropriation/adjustment of the decreetal amount has not been followed.
He further submits that the Executing Court has apparently adjusted the amount directly towards the principle and thereafter towards the interest.

(b) He further refers to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Gurpreet Singh Vs.
Union of India reported in 2006 (8) SCC 457 and relying upon the law enunciated in the said judgment at paragraph Nos.53 and 54 submits that the amount ought to have been appropriated firstly towards the interest then towards the costs and thereafter towards the principle.

entities.text:
Gurpreet Singh Vs.
Union of India reported in 2006 (8) SCC 457
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further NC: 2024:KHC-D:9816 submits that it was the obligation on the part of the respondent-authorities to have stated before the Executing Court as to how the money paid by them was to be adjusted.
He refers to the Clause (c) of Sub Rule (3) of Rule 1 Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'CPC').

entities.text: Clause (c) of Sub Rule (3) of Rule 1 Order XXI
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: Thus, he submits that the calculation arrived at by the Executing Court apart from the erroneous is also illegal in view of the aforesaid provisions of law.
Hence, seeks for allowing the petition.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent through Video Conferencing on the other hand submits that the very filing of the present execution petition is not maintainable inasmuch as, once the execution petition is closed, there is no question of re-opening it.

He relies upon the very same judgment of Gurpreet Singh (supra) to contend that the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court referred to above is applicable only in respect of the pending cases and not in the closed execution petitions.
Thus, he submits that the respondent-authorities are not liable to pay any amount whatsoever.
Heard.
Perused the records.

3 6. Entitlement of the petitioner/land looser to the compensation which includes payment of land value, 30% solatium, 12% of additional market value, 9% of interest for the initial one year and 15%
interest thereafter till the payment, is a statutory requirement to be complied with by the acquiring authorities.
There cannot be any dispute about the same.
7. The entitlement of the petitioner/land looser has never be under challenged.

Though, the first execution petition filed by the petitioners in EP No.538/1997 is admittedly closed on 20.08.1998,
the present execution petition in EP No.151/2012 is filed in view of the order dated 24.02.2012 passed by this Court in CRP No.1115/2011 wherein, this Court has held that the petitioner would be entitled for interest on solatium and additional market value.
This order dated 24.02.2012 has not been questioned or challenged by the respondent- authorities.

So much so, the respondent-authorities have not even questioned the filing of the present execution NC:
2024:KHC-D:9816 petition by the petitioner/land looser before the Executing Court, till date.
As such, the objection now raised at the last leg of the proceedings regarding the maintainability of the present execution petition cannot be countenanced.

8. Necessary to note that it is the petitioner/land looser who is before this Court being aggrieved by the calculation of amount due made in the present execution petition in E.P.No.151/2012 and not the respondent- authorities.

In that view of the matter, submission of learned counsel for the respondent objecting to very filing of execution petition, and the order passed therein cannot be heard.
9. Coming to the merits of the submission with regard to calculation is concerned, paragraph No.53 of the judgment passed in the case of Gurpreet Singh (supra) is extracted hereunder;

"Thus, on the whole, we are satisfied that the essential ratio in Prem Nath Kapur1 on appropriation being at different stages if justified though if at a particular stage there is Prem Nath Kapur V. National Fertilizers Corpn. Of India Ltd., (1996) 2 SCC 71:
1 9 9 9 5 S u p p ( 5 ) S C R 7 9 0 N C : 2 0 2 4 : K H C - D : 9 8 1 6 a s h o r t f a l l , t h e awardee-decree-holder would be entitled to appropriate the same on the general principle of appropriation, first towards interest, then towards costs and then towards the principal, unless, of course, the deposit is indicated to be towards specified heads by the judgment-debtor while making the deposit intimating the decree-holder of his intention.

entities.text: Prem Nath Kapur V. National Fertilizers Corpn. Of India Ltd., (1996) 2 SCC 71
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
We, thus, approve the ratio of Prem Nath Kapur on the aspect of appropriation."
10.

Further provisions of Clause (c) of Sub Rule (3) of Rule 1 Order XXI of CPC also mandates the respondent/Judgment Debtor to intimate as to the mode of paying the money, whether towards principal, cost or interest.

entities.text: Clause (c) of Sub Rule (3) of Rule 1 Order XXI
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: This being the legal requirement in the cases of payment of money/recovery of money, and the same not having been adhereto, in the considered view of this Court the Executing Court has erred in declining to appreciate the calculation submitted by the petitioner/land looser.

In that view of the matter, the following:
ORDER i) Petition is allowed.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9816 ii) Order dated 12.08.2014 passed in EP No.151/2012 is set aside.

iii) Matter is remitted to the Executing Court to recalculate the amount payable by the respondent-authorities keeping in mind the law enunciated in the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Gurpreet Singh (supra) at paragraph No.53 and also provisions of the Clause (c) Sub Rule (3) of Rule 1 Order XXI of CPC.

entities.text: Clause (c) Sub Rule (3) of Rule 1 Order XXI
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: iv) Parties are also at liberty to submit their calculations; the Executing Court shall after affording opportunity, pass appropriate orders.

v) Since the matter is of the year 1975, the Executing Court shall endeavor to dispose off the execution petition within an outer limit of six(6) months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
Since the parties are present through their counsel, they shall appear before the Executing Court on 14.08.2024 without further notice.

"Thus, on the whole, we are satisfied that the essential ratio in Prem Nath Kapur1 on appropriation being at different stages if justified though if at a particular stage there is Prem Nath Kapur V. National Fertilizers Corpn. Of India Ltd., (1996) 2 SCC 71:

Further provisions of Clause (c) of Sub Rule (3) of Rule 1 Order XXI of CPC also mandates the respondent/Judgment Debtor to intimate as to the mode of paying the money, whether towards principal, cost or interest.
This being the legal requirement in the cases of payment of money/recovery of money, and the same not having been adhereto, in the considered view of this Court the Executing Court has erred in declining to appreciate the calculation submitted by the petitioner/land looser.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In that view of the matter, the following:
ORDER i) Petition is allowed.

iv) Parties are also at liberty to submit their calculations; the Executing Court shall after affording opportunity, pass appropriate orders.
